lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The house of cards is no longer merely wobbling - it is shedding pieces by the handful. Toronto's 4-3 loss to Columbus on Nov. 21 extended the losing streak to nine games, with two late third-period goals in 52 seconds turning another lead into another defeat. The Leafs are 8-14, 13th in the Eastern Conference, 14 points out of the pace, and the four-game slide listed in the standings understates the broader collapse. Anthony Stolarz made 31 saves against the Blue Jackets, but goaltending cannot keep rescuing a team whose structure keeps springing leaks. The injury list is brutal: Kirill Marchenko remains out with a lower-body injury, while Jack Roslovic is day-to-day; Marchenko had 14 points in his first 14 games. Jim Hiller's line juggling now looks less like strategy than panic. At 7:30 p.m. in New York, the Islanders visit is a referendum on whether Toronto can finally stop the bleeding.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The Blue Jays' offseason was supposed to begin with a statement, and it did - just not the one Toronto wanted. Tarik Skubal chose the Mets on a record nine-year, $450 million contract after Toronto reportedly offered more than $400 million, leaving the Jays with proof of ambition but no ace to show for it. That is the sharp edge of a finished season worth only -2.0 points: the problem is not willingness to spend, but converting urgency into impact. Dylan Cease remains the rotation's anchor, yet one anchor does not make a seaworthy staff. The lineup, meanwhile, still needs another authoritative bat; the signature swing of Toronto's best slugger cannot carry the whole enterprise. No consolation prize will do. Watch the next move: whether Toronto turns its Skubal money toward Seiya Suzuki and pitching depth before camp opens March 25 at Yankee Stadium.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors beat the Pistons 105-102, moving to 6-10 on the season. They sit 4th in atlantic division, and the standings race sharpens a little every night. Before that, the club lost to the Wizards 99-103. There is runway left in the schedule, and the work on rotations and matchups matters as much as the scoreboard. Next up: vs. Bucks on Mon 11/23 at 7:30 PM ET. Around the NBA, the offseason machinery is already whirring - front offices are mapping out draft boards, free-agent target lists are being quietly circulated, and cap projections are being stress-tested against every conceivable scenario. For the Toronto Raptors, the conversation centers on which direction the rebuild takes next and whether the draft lottery delivers the kind of franchise-altering talent that can accelerate the timeline.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The season's pulse is faint but steady, and Monday night offers Washington a chance to make noise before the calendar turns unforgiving. Brandon Aiyuk has emerged as a legitimate possibility, with Washington reportedly considering him after his expected release - a tempting gamble for a receiver room already without Terry McLaurin. At 3-5-1, third in the NFC East and 2.5 games behind, the Commanders have won two of their last three, including a 24-21 escape against the Giants on Nov. 12, but the margin for error remains microscopic. Jayden Daniels practiced fully despite a left elbow issue, while Rachaad White is questionable with a heel injury and Jacory Croskey-Merritt could return from injured reserve. Jonathan Allen's return to Washington adds its own edge. Beat Cincinnati at 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, and Washington can start dreaming big again; lose, and the climb becomes nearly vertical.

article.title: Maple Leafs Visit Islanders Amid Nine-Game Slide
paragraphs: The Leafs visit the Islanders tonight at 7:30 p.m. on Sportsnet, carrying a nine-game losing streak into New York. Anthony Stolarz is projected to start against Ilya Sorokin, while Jack Roslovic is day-to-day with an upper-body injury. Toronto is 8-14 and 13th in the Eastern Conference.

The Jays are looking ahead after reports that their offer for Tarik Skubal exceeded $400 million, only to fall short. Their next scheduled game is the March 25 regular-season opener at the Yankees. The Raptors host the Bucks at 7:30 p.m., with Bittle, Leonard and Barrett out and Murray-Boyles day-to-day; Toronto is 6-10. The Commanders, 3-5-1 and third in the NFC East, host the Bengals at 8:15 p.m. on ESPN. Patrick, Robertson and White are questionable.
